V4A_KEY_LIFECYCLE_DESIGN.problem: v3 used ONE long-lived secret with window_id in the HMAC MESSAGE. A holder of that secret plus ledger access can derive bucket keys for every window the secret ever covered - unbounded historical linkability.
V4A_KEY_LIFECYCLE_DESIGN.requirement: Compromise of the CURRENTLY ACTIVE key must not permit deriving bucket identifiers for an unbounded history of EXPIRED windows.
V4A_KEY_LIFECYCLE_DESIGN.chosenDesign: FORWARD-SECURE HASH RATCHET over a single Vault secret, with periodic re-seed.

construction.bucketKey: HMAC-SHA256(K_epoch, 'fda028-bucket-v1|' || normalized_prefix) truncated to 16 bytes; the epoch is IMPLICIT in the key, not merely mixed into the message
construction.advance: strictly wall-clock driven: advance only while stored_epoch < epoch_of(now()). A caller cannot force an advance; epoch is a pure function of request time.
construction.catchUpCap: bounded iterations; if the stored key is staler than the cap, RE-SEED with fresh gen_random_bytes(32) instead of iterating
construction.reseed: every R epochs (configurable), replace the key with fresh randomness instead of ratcheting

V4A_KEY_LIFECYCLE_DESIGN.whyThisSatisfiesBlocker3: HMAC is one-way, so K_{n+1} cannot yield K_n. A holder of the live key can derive FUTURE keys but NO past ones. Past-window bucket identifiers are therefore underivable from a current-key compromise, which is exactly the stated requirement.
V4A_KEY_LIFECYCLE_DESIGN.whyItFitsTheDOCUMENTED VaultAPI: It needs only vault.update_secret(uuid, secret, name, description), which IS documented. It never calls vault.create_secret at request time (whose signature, uniqueness scoping and concurrent-creation behaviour the v2/v3 reviews found UNVERIFIED), and it never needs secret DELETION - which Supabase documents no method for. The old key value is destroyed by being OVERWRITTEN in place.
V4A_KEY_LIFECYCLE_DESIGN.honestLimitation_backupsAndPITR: NO CLAIM OF CRYPTOGRAPHIC DELETION FROM BACKUPS. A historical backup or PITR snapshot containing K_n lets an attacker ratchet FORWARD from epoch n. The re-seed bounds that exposure to at most R epochs rather than unbounded, but it does not eliminate it. This is stated rather than claimed away, per the governing instruction.

comparisonToAlternatives.v3_longLivedSecret: REJECTED - unbounded past and future linkability from one compromise.
comparisonToAlternatives.independentRandomPerEpochKeys: Strictly better against backup exposure (a backup leaks only its own epoch), but requires per-epoch secret CREATION and DELETION. Deletion is undocumented in Supabase Vault and creation semantics are unverified. Rejected as unverifiable, not as undesirable.
comparisonToAlternatives.kdfFromLongLivedMaster: REJECTED - master compromise derives every epoch, failing the requirement outright.

V4A_KEY_LIFECYCLE_DESIGN.keyMaterialStorage: Vault only. The limiter schema stores only the non-secret epoch number and re-seed anchor. No key material in any application table.
V4A_KEY_LIFECYCLE_DESIGN.testability: The ratchet MATH is a pure function testable locally without Vault. The Vault read/update I/O has no local equivalent in disposable Postgres and will be recorded as VAULT_IO: UNVERIFIED_LOCALLY rather than asserted as passing.

findings.postgres_canonicalizes_mapped_hex_form: '::ffff:c000:263' renders as '::ffff:192.0.2.99' - both textual forms of an IPv4-mapped address converge
findings.dotted_tail_extraction: substring(host(addr) from '([0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3})$') extracts the embedded IPv4 and is NULL for native IPv6
findings.set_masklen_family_sensitivity: set_masklen(addr,64) RAISES 'invalid mask length' on an IPv4 address - the family branch must precede masking

V4A_NORMALIZATION_PRIMITIVE_EVIDENCE.plannedRule: if family=6 AND mapped -> unwrap to IPv4 then apply the IPv4 prefix; elif family=4 -> IPv4 prefix; else -> IPv6 prefix. Unwrap strictly BEFORE any generic IPv6 prefixing.

V4A_IPV6_PREFIX_DECISION.v3ReviewerObjection: Modern mobile OSes rotate RFC 4941 privacy addresses automatically, so /128 effectively voids reset continuity for ordinary IPv6 mobile guests on routine reconnects - not only for deliberate evasion.
V4A_IPV6_PREFIX_DECISION.rationale: RFC 4941 privacy-address rotation changes the low 64 bits (the interface identifier) and preserves the /64 prefix. /64 therefore defeats the DOMINANT real-world rotation vector while avoiding the over-collapse risk of /48, where an ISP assigning /64s to different subscribers from a shared larger block would lump unrelated people together. For an accessibility app, over-collapsing means locking out real users, so the asymmetry favours the narrower prefix.
V4A_IPV6_PREFIX_DECISION.residual: In-delegation rotation across multiple /64s within a subscriber's /56 or /48 remains possible. Bounding it requires hosted IPv6 evidence, which is still OPEN.
